description: Extension of calculus to functions of several variables. Covers partial derivatives, multiple integrals, vector calculus, and the fundamental theorems of Green, Stokes, and the Divergence Theorem.

modules.title: Vectors and the Geometry of Space

concepts.title: Three-Dimensional Coordinate Systems
learning_objectives: Plot points and describe regions in three-dimensional Cartesian coordinates
Compute distances between points in R³
Write equations of spheres and identify their center and radius

concepts.title: Vectors in Three Dimensions
learning_objectives: Represent vectors in R³ in component form and perform vector arithmetic
Compute the magnitude and unit vector in the direction of a given vector
Express vectors in terms of the standard basis vectors i, j, k

concepts.title: The Cross Product
learning_objectives: Compute the cross product of two vectors using the determinant formula
Interpret the cross product geometrically as area and direction (right-hand rule)
Apply the cross product to find the area of a parallelogram and a triangle in R³

concepts.title: Lines and Planes in Space
learning_objectives: Write parametric and symmetric equations of a line in R³
Write the equation of a plane given a point and a normal vector
Compute the distance from a point to a plane and the angle between two planes

concepts.title: Space Curves and Parametric Equations
learning_objectives: Define and graph vector-valued functions r(t) = ⟨x(t), y(t), z(t)⟩
Compute limits and determine continuity of vector-valued functions
Parameterize common space curves (helix, circle in R³)

concepts.title: Derivatives and Integrals of Vector Functions
learning_objectives: Differentiate vector-valued functions component-wise
Interpret r'(t) as the tangent vector and compute the unit tangent vector
Integrate vector-valued functions to find position from velocity

concepts.title: Arc Length and Curvature
learning_objectives: Compute arc length of a space curve using integration
Define and compute the curvature κ of a space curve
Find the unit normal and binormal vectors (TNB frame)

concepts.title: Functions of Several Variables
learning_objectives: Evaluate functions of two and three variables and determine their domains
Sketch level curves for functions of two variables
Describe level surfaces for functions of three variables

concepts.title: Limits and Continuity in Several Variables
learning_objectives: Evaluate limits of multivariable functions along different paths
Prove a limit does not exist by finding two paths with different limits
Apply the Squeeze Theorem in multiple variables

concepts.title: Partial Derivatives
learning_objectives: Compute partial derivatives by treating other variables as constants
Compute second-order and mixed partial derivatives
Apply Clairaut's theorem on equality of mixed partials

concepts.title: The Chain Rule for Multivariable Functions
learning_objectives: Apply the multivariable chain rule for functions of functions
Draw and use tree diagrams to organize chain rule computations
Compute implicit partial derivatives using the chain rule

concepts.title: Directional Derivatives and the Gradient
learning_objectives: Compute the gradient vector ∇f for scalar-valued functions
Compute directional derivatives using the gradient and a unit direction vector
Interpret the gradient as the direction of steepest ascent and its magnitude as the maximum rate of change

concepts.title: Tangent Planes and Linear Approximation
learning_objectives: Find the equation of the tangent plane to a surface at a point
Use the tangent plane for linear approximation of multivariable functions
Compute the total differential and estimate error in calculated quantities

concepts.title: Extrema of Multivariable Functions
learning_objectives: Find critical points of functions of two variables
Apply the second derivative test (using the Hessian determinant) to classify critical points
Find absolute extrema on closed bounded regions

concepts.title: Lagrange Multipliers
learning_objectives: Set up and solve constrained optimization problems using Lagrange multipliers
Handle optimization with multiple constraints
Interpret the Lagrange multiplier λ as the rate of change of the optimum with respect to the constraint

concepts.title: Double Integrals over Rectangular Regions
learning_objectives: Evaluate double integrals as iterated integrals using Fubini's theorem
Interpret double integrals as volume under a surface
Apply Fubini's theorem to change the order of integration over rectangles

concepts.title: Double Integrals over General Regions
learning_objectives: Set up iterated integrals over Type I and Type II regions
Change the order of integration by re-describing the region
Compute areas and volumes using double integrals

concepts.title: Double Integrals in Polar Coordinates
learning_objectives: Convert double integrals from Cartesian to polar coordinates with the Jacobian r
Set up and evaluate double integrals in polar coordinates over appropriate regions
Recognize regions that are simpler to describe in polar coordinates

concepts.title: Applications of Double Integrals
learning_objectives: Compute mass, center of mass, and moments of inertia of planar laminae with variable density
Compute surface area using double integrals
Apply double integrals to probability (joint density functions)

concepts.title: Triple Integrals in Cartesian Coordinates
learning_objectives: Set up and evaluate triple integrals as iterated integrals
Describe three-dimensional regions with appropriate integration limits
Compute volume and mass of solid regions using triple integrals

concepts.title: Triple Integrals in Cylindrical Coordinates
learning_objectives: Convert between Cartesian and cylindrical coordinates
Set up and evaluate triple integrals in cylindrical coordinates with Jacobian r
Identify solids best described in cylindrical coordinates

concepts.title: Triple Integrals in Spherical Coordinates
learning_objectives: Convert between Cartesian and spherical coordinates
Set up and evaluate triple integrals in spherical coordinates with Jacobian ρ² sin φ
Identify solids best described in spherical coordinates (spheres, cones)

concepts.title: Change of Variables and the Jacobian
learning_objectives: Compute the Jacobian determinant for a general change of variables
Apply the change of variables formula for double and triple integrals
Design custom transformations to simplify integration regions

concepts.title: Vector Fields
learning_objectives: Define and sketch two-dimensional and three-dimensional vector fields
Identify gradient vector fields (conservative fields)
Compute the divergence and curl of a vector field

concepts.title: Line Integrals of Scalar and Vector Fields
learning_objectives: Evaluate line integrals of scalar functions along parameterized curves
Evaluate line integrals of vector fields (work integrals) along parameterized curves
Interpret line integrals as work done by a force along a path

concepts.title: Conservative Fields and Path Independence
learning_objectives: Determine whether a vector field is conservative by checking curl = 0
Find a potential function for a conservative vector field
Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals

concepts.title: Green's Theorem
learning_objectives: State Green's theorem relating a line integral to a double integral
Apply Green's theorem to evaluate line integrals by computing double integrals
Use Green's theorem to compute areas of regions bounded by curves

concepts.title: Flux Form of Green's Theorem
learning_objectives: State and apply the flux form of Green's theorem
Compute the outward flux of a vector field across a closed curve
Relate the flux form to the divergence of the vector field

concepts.title: Parametric Surfaces
learning_objectives: Parameterize surfaces in R³ using two parameters
Compute the tangent plane to a parametric surface
Compute the surface area element dS from a parameterization

concepts.title: Surface Integrals of Scalar and Vector Fields
learning_objectives: Evaluate surface integrals of scalar functions over parametric surfaces
Evaluate flux integrals of vector fields through oriented surfaces
Choose and apply the correct orientation (outward normal) for flux integrals

modules.title: Stokes' Theorem and the Divergence Theorem

concepts.title: Stokes' Theorem
learning_objectives: State Stokes' theorem relating a surface integral of curl to a line integral
Apply Stokes' theorem to convert between surface and line integrals
Verify Stokes' theorem by computing both sides for a given example

concepts.title: The Divergence Theorem
learning_objectives: State the Divergence Theorem relating a surface flux integral to a triple integral of divergence
Apply the Divergence Theorem to evaluate flux integrals over closed surfaces
Interpret the Divergence Theorem physically as conservation of flow

concepts.title: Unifying the Fundamental Theorems
learning_objectives: Identify Green's, Stokes', and the Divergence Theorem as instances of the generalized Stokes' theorem
Select the appropriate theorem for a given vector calculus problem
Interpret all three theorems as relating an integral over a boundary to an integral over the enclosed region

projects.title: Optimizing a Satellite Ground Station Network
projects.description: Use Lagrange multipliers to optimize the placement of ground stations on an ellipsoidal Earth model subject to coverage constraints. Compute surface areas covered using surface integrals.
learning_objectives: Formulate a constrained optimization problem on a curved surface
Apply Lagrange multipliers with multiple constraints
Compute surface integrals over portions of an ellipsoid

projects.title: Verifying Maxwell's Equations in Integral Form
projects.description: Given specific electric and magnetic field configurations, verify Gauss's Law and Faraday's Law using the Divergence Theorem and Stokes' Theorem respectively.
learning_objectives: Compute divergence and curl of physical vector fields
Apply the Divergence Theorem to verify Gauss's Law for specific charge distributions
Apply Stokes' Theorem to verify Faraday's Law for specific field configurations

projects.title: Center of Mass of a Variable-Density Solid
projects.description: Compute the center of mass of a solid with non-uniform density using triple integrals in multiple coordinate systems. Compare the efficiency of Cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical approaches.
learning_objectives: Set up mass and moment integrals for a three-dimensional solid
Select the most efficient coordinate system for a given geometry
Evaluate triple integrals in all three coordinate systems and verify consistency
